evidence: The visible cuff remains attached to the stationary leg while the other unweighted leg crosses. This does not demonstrate the required loaded hip adduction.
The highlight travels over the front thigh/shin of the unweighted moving leg rather than the inner-thigh adductors of the cuffed working leg.
Several partial crossing pulses occur before the finish; trimming cannot fix the wrong attachment and working limb.
limitations: Inspected two ordered 3 fps delivery sheets; not continuous playback or trainer review.
reviews.nextApproach: Build a still with one clearly cuffed working ankle beside the low pulley and the inner thigh highlighted. Animate ONLY that cuffed leg across the midline and fully back.

evidence: The cable descends from above and the elbows/upper arms lower toward the sides in a behind-neck pulldown. This is not an overhead elbow-extension movement against a cable originating behind/below.
The orange graphic primarily occupies the upper/middle back and rear shoulder areas rather than the posterior upper-arm triceps bellies.
There is also an extra lowering phase after the initial return. No correct triceps-extension cycle exists to trim.
limitations: Inspected two ordered 3 fps delivery sheets; not continuous playback or trainer review.
reviews.nextApproach: Use a reviewed rear-side still of upper arms fixed elevated beside the head, elbows deeply bent, hands behind the crown and rope attached to a low cable behind. Animate forearms only to full extension and back.
